digest.component_or_area: pytest fixture teardown and snapshot cleanup
propositions: Snapshot teardown fixture _remove_readonly_run_snapshots uses Path.rglob to recursively scan tmp_path, causing traversal into concurrent live lock directories like .ticket-write.lock.d that disappear mid-walk, raising FileNotFoundError on Python 3.11 but not 3.12.

Python 3.11 pathlib.Path.rglob caches directory entries from parent scans and does not suppress FileNotFoundError when a cached child directory vanishes before descent, while Python 3.12+ delegates to os.walk which ignores scandir errors.

The canonical store write lifecycle at src/rebar/_store/lock.py intentionally creates and removes .ticket-write.lock.d during LockHandle.release(), racing against the fixture's broad recursive scan when tests/conftest.py materializes tuple(tmp_path.rglob(...)).

Repair replaced broad Path.rglob with os.walk(..., onerror=...) to ignore only FileNotFoundError for concurrently vanished entries while re-raising other walk errors, preserving exact .rebar/run_snapshots discovery and read-only publication semantics.

Ambient Path(dirpath) factory calls at tests/conftest.py:353,358 and src/rebar/llm/workflow/snapshot.py:145 raise NotImplementedError on Python 3.11 when os.name is monkeypatched to 'nt' by concurrent Windows-simulation tests, requiring scoped concrete-path construction through the test harness.

Deterministic synchronization barrier at tests/unit/test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py proved root cause and repair by: reaching FileNotFoundError RED state before fix, returning GREEN after os.walk conversion, reverting to RED under exact-defect mutation, and verifying non-disappearance errors remain visible.
